title: Coarse location and magnitude matching retained a late timing excess near deep earthquakes in ComCat, 2001-2024
abstract: We tested whether a reported depth contrast in nearby earthquake timing remains within coarse location and magnitude groups. We reused a fixed ComCat snapshot and 646 shallow and 99 deep M6.5 to below 8 centers in 2001-2024. Neighbors had magnitude at least 5.5 and chord distance at most 200 km. Late days were (7,30] and early days were (1,7]. Matching used 20-degree location cells and three magnitude bands. The Mantel-Haenszel late-versus-early odds ratio for deep versus shallow centers was 2.43. Its conditional 95% three-year block interval was 1.22 to 8.07. Seven groups in four location cells supplied the comparison, with 178 shallow and 25 deep pairs. The result remained positive with a shifted grid and 40-degree cells. The interval included equal odds at 100 km. The M6 neighbor check was poorly identified. Thus coarse location matching did not explain away the association at 200 km. Sparse counts, background activity, large cells, future-dependent center selection, shared events and revised data limit inference. This is a follow-up on the same data as a prior campaign result, not independent confirmation or proof of a slower physical decay at depth. The package includes new code, aggregate evidence, source hashes, a figure and an independent numerical audit.

display.caption: Late-versus-early timing odds ratios and conditional three-year block limits. The dotted M6 interval is unbounded. The right panel shows how many pairs lie in informative primary strata. The comparison uses only four geographic cells.

citations.reason: Same source snapshot, center rules and windows. We add a within-location and magnitude timing test with new code. This is not independent confirmation.
